APRIL 27, 1933.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C & S. B. REGISTRY
No. D 4743
Date 27 / 4 / 33

CHEN TU HSUI

Chen Tu Hsui and other Lee I neng persons:

ARREST OF CHEN TU HSUI AND OTHERS.

Mr. Li Tsung Lien (李宗蓮), a former student of Fuhien University, was arrested in the Library of the Shanghai Chamber of Commerce on suspicion of being a Communist. He is now detained in the Public Safety Bureau. Dr. Tsai Yuan Pei yesterday sent the following letter to Chin Chi, President of the Executive Yuan:-
On suspicion of being a Communist, Li Tsung Lien, a former student of Fuhien University, was recently arrested by the Public Safety Bureau of the Municipality of the City of Shanghai. The latter, who has been examined by the People's Rights Protection League, was remanded to the Public Safety Bureau to see Li, but was refused admittance because of the importance of the case.
Mr. Li, it will be remembered, was dismissed by the Communist Party in the eighteenth year of the Chinese Republic. Since then, he has been living on books on Chinese Academies. During the past two years, he spent most of his time among the libraries in Shanghai. He can not be charged with desiring to injure the Republic of China.
I request you to instruct the Public Safety Bureau of the Municipality of Greater Shanghai to release Li Tsung Lieng immediately or to hand him over to the Shanghai District Court for public trial.

China Times (Nanking telegram):

THE CHEN TOU SEU CASE.

The Nanking District Court delivered the following judgment in the Chen Tou Seu case yesterday:-
Chen Tou Seu and Bang Jih Ts have been sentenced to 15 years' imprisonment and 15 years' deprivation of civil rights on a charge of subverting the Government with written propaganda.
Tang Ts Ping (王子平) and Ho Sh Tong have been sentenced to 5 years' imprisonment and 7 years' deprivation of civil rights for abetting Chen and Bang in disseminating subversive propaganda against the Government.
Wang Ju (王武), Pi Yih Van (濮一凡) and Wang Zau Kyuin (王兆年) have been sentenced to two and half years' imprisonment and three years' deprivation of civil rights on a charge of founding organizations with the object of endangering the Republic.
Liang Yu Kwang (梁有光) and Wang Kying Teng (王經堂) have been acquitted.
Chen and Bang were allowed to read books and to receive callers in prison.
Chen is considering an appeal against the sentence.

Date April 16, 1933.

Subject (in full) Arrest of three communist suspects in the Chinese Chamber
of Commerce, N.Honan Road.

Made by... D.I.Kuh Pro-nwa Forwarded by.

With reference to the endorsement of the Officer i/c
Special Branch on the attached report dated April 8, 1933, from
West Hongkew Station on the subject of the arrest of three
communist suspects in the Chinese Chamber of Commerce, North
Honan Road, information from the Chinese Authorities obtained
through Supt. Tan reveal that the antecedents of the three
arrested suspects are as follows :-
(1) Loo Tsung Loong (卢宗龙), age 30, native of Changsha, Hunan,
a savant. Was formerly a member of the Hunan
Provincial Committee of the Communist Party and one
of the leaders who participated in the movement of
establishing labour unions in Shanghai. At the 6th
General Meeting of Representatives of the Chinese
Communist Party, he was appointed Chief of the
Central Propaganda Department and concurrently member
of the Special Administration Bureau of the Party.
He was later appointed Chief-Secretary of the National
Labour Union of the Communist Party. As he was not
in agreement with the plans of the Executive Clique,
following the convention of the 4th Plenary Session
of the Communist Party, he left the said Clique and
organized the Extra-Ordinary Committee of the Communist
Party of which he became the Chairman. Subsequently
he proceeded to the North and organized the so-called
"Northern Bureau". After his return to Shanghai and
following the upset of various communist organizations,
he organized a "New Central" of the Communist Party
and appointed himself Chief of the Organization
Department.

(2) Wong Tuh (王 体 ): Age 22, native of King-hwa (金 華 ),
Chekiang. Ex-Chief of the Organization Department
of the Chekiang Provincial Committee of the
Communist Party. Wanted by the Chekiang Authorities
for having directed the peasants' movement at King-
hwa, Chekiang. After leaving the Executive Clique,
he became Chief of the Propaganda Department of the
"Extra-ordinary Committee" organized by Loo Tsoung
Loong, 1st named, which position he held up to the
time of his arrest.

(3) Tsui Ying (朱 英 ): Age 35, native of Au Shiang (澳 湘 ),
Hunan. Formerly participated in peasants' move-
ments. At the time of his arrest, he was Chief
Secretary of the "Extra-ordinary Committee".

The abovementioned three accused were arrested
at about 5 p.m. April 8 by the Chinese authorities in the
Chinese Chamber of Commerce Building, North Honan Road, for
attempting to hold an inauguration meeting of the "Extra-
Ordinary Committee of the Right Wing of the Chinese Communist
Party" in the library on the said premises. Following
their arrest, they were removed to the headquarters of the
Public Safety Bureau where they are at present detained.

The particulars of the above arrest have been
recorded by this office for future reference.

REPORT
Hongkew Station,
Date. April 8, 1933

Subject (in full) Arrest of three suspected Communists in the Chinese Chamber
of Commerce, North Honan Road.

Made by I. S. I. Ash Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,

At 4-20 p.m. April 8, Detectives Wong Yun Tsing (王文俊)
and Wong Ching Nan (孔慶南) of the Bureau of Public Safety,
Nantao reported at this station that they were in receipt of in-
formation to the effect that an attempt would be made to hold a
communist meeting in the library of the Chinese Chamber of Comm-
erce, North Honan Road at 5 p.m. even date. Accordingly a party
of police from this station proceeded to the scene and were posted
on the road outside the Chamber as a precautionary measure against
any anticipated demonstration.

At 5 p.m. the Police in the vicinity were informed that the
meeting would not take place. From subsequent enquiries made by
detectives, it was ascertained that the P... representatives
had arrested three male Chinese inside the Chamber as suspected
communists and had taken them direct to Nantao in a raiding van
which was seen to leave the premises at about 5 p.m.

No particulars could be obtained regarding the identity of
the arrested persons and no application was made by the Chinese
Authorities for a S.M.P. escort to accompany the vehicle.

D. I.C. "C", A.D.C. "C" and Supt. Robertson informed.
